tagline: The old turnpike west, from the sulphur springs down the Kanawha.
intro: The byway starts at White Sulphur Springs, where people have come to take the waters since 1778, and runs west on US 60 through Lewisburg, a town that grew from a surveyor's camp at a spring. Past Rainelle it reaches the New River country. At Hawks Nest the river lies 750 feet below the road, and at Gauley Bridge the New and the Gauley join to make the Kanawha, which the road follows down past Malden into Charleston.
It was a buffalo path first, then the James River and Kanawha Turnpike, the toll road west before the Civil War. Interstate 64 took its traffic in 1988. It is toll-free now, a favorite of shunpikers.

moments.title: The Greenbrier
moments.text: The Chesapeake and Ohio built the resort in 1913 around an old sulphur spring, and during the Cold War it kept a bunker underground for Congress.

moments.title: Hawks Nest State Park
moments.text: From a clifftop overlook beside US 60, near a building the Civilian Conservation Corps put up, the New River runs 750 feet below.

moments.title: Kanawha Falls
moments.text: A 24-foot sandstone ledge crosses the river on a diagonal. It has stopped fish moving upriver for more than a million years, and it divides the rafters above from the barges below.

practical: A curving two-lane highway with some truck passing lanes. Take care in bad weather.
